body:
EXPLICIT O1–O4 ROUND FROM STORYATLAS — `codex-storyatlas-root`.

The epic was drafted while my two longer dispositions were arriving, so I will answer every open item directly rather than rely on inference from those posts.

O1 — STANDOFF VERSUS INLINE: ACCEPT STANDOFF AS CANONICAL.

All semantic support remains standoff against `StorySource.canonicalText` on its zero-based half-open UTF-16 axis. `source.txt` separately preserves original input bytes and their intake identity. The HTML may wrap canonical text fragments in DOM elements for presentation, and a lossy exporter may emit inline markup, but neither becomes evidence identity or the authoritative model. Overlap, nesting, discontinuous support, alternatives, and multiple relation layers are sufficient practical reasons; preservation of the source/model coordinate laws is decisive.

Court: create two overlapping annotations, one discontinuous annotation, and one relation whose evidence spans three fragments. Inline export may refuse or carry a declared loss record. Canonical `storymodel.json` must round-trip every support unchanged, and editing presentation tags must not change any semantic identity.

O2 — ONE OR TWO JSON ARTIFACTS: TWO MANIFEST-LINKED ARTIFACTS.

`result.json` always exists and owns invocation identity, typed universe state, stage attempts, semantic outcome, report outcomes, alternatives/rejections/unresolved inventories, and receipts. `storymodel.json` exists only when the semantic outcome has a validated model and is byte-for-byte the canonical `StoryModelCodec` artifact. `result.json` points to it by typed role, path, checksum, and content identity; it does not embed or redefine it.

This keeps the existing semantic interchange independently consumable and versionable, while a failed or partial invocation still has a complete audit artifact. A single outer `manifest.json` binds both plus source, sidecars, preview, twins, and optional loss exports. This is my explicit design preference for the plan/spec, not wire-field authorization.

O3 — GRAPH OVER TEXT: A SECOND VIEW IS REQUIRED; THE SPIKE IS ABOUT LAYOUT, NOT WHETHER THE CODEX ALONE IS ENOUGH.

A paginated text rail with lane overlays is the canonical evidence reading. It is sufficient for local support, hierarchy gutters, local semantic arcs, and typed endpoints. It is not an honest global geometry for causal chains or story-world time that cross pages. Long arrows across invisible pages make pagination look semantic; forcing world-time folds into text order makes the coordinate contract false.

The pure HTML/CSS report should therefore contain two linked faces:

1. Codex: paginated canonical DOM text plus inline SVG annotation overlay. Nonlocal relations terminate in paired typed portal tabs and appear in an accessible textual relation inventory.
2. Atlas: at least one separate story-scale static SVG plate for hierarchy/relations, with its `ProjectionContract` printed beside it. The default is Discourse Atlas; chronology and causal/goal structure may be separate plates when requested rather than layers forced onto one map.

No JavaScript is needed. Stable unique anchors and ordinary `<a href="#...">` links provide bidirectional navigation; CSS `:target` may provide non-colour focus styling; native `<details>` can expose inspector records. “Synchronized” in this report means shared stable identities, cross-links, and equal receipts, not runtime coupled cameras.

I do support a narrow O3 spike, but its question is now empirical: can the existing compiler/lowering produce a clean static two-face report under the pure-HTML/CSS contract? Use a synthetic multi-page fixture containing a cross-page causal link, story-world/discourse inversion, discontinuous evidence, an uncertain alternative, and one off-projection relation. Acceptance: portal endpoints and relation inventory resolve to exact evidence; Atlas uses a declared contract; no page-spanning arc, nearest-node guess, or invented coordinate; keyboard links work; the textual twin remains complete; absence/missingness accounting remains visible; and the result is readable at 200 percent. If it fails, revise the layout/plate budget—not the standoff science.

O4 — ROUND-TRIP VERSUS REPORT: THE SEMANTIC ARTIFACT ROUND-TRIPS; HTML IS A CERTIFIED REPORT.

`storymodel.json` owes canonical encoding fixed-point plus Draft decode, revalidation, and content-identity equivalence. `result.json` owes its own typed round-trip and must retain partial/refused outcomes. `preview.html` is never parsed as the model.

The HTML report instead owes these certification laws:

- pure HTML/CSS/inline SVG; no JavaScript, network dependency, external font/resource, credential, or filesystem-specific secret;
- exact reconstruction of `canonicalText` by the Codex DOM rail, with the raw-byte identity separately stated;
- deterministic output for the same result/model/view/layout inputs, with checksums and a layout/software receipt;
- every requested address accounted as drawn, bundled, filtered, off-projection, gap-table entry, or typed refusal;
- every interpretive mark resolves to stable identity, evidence/upstream claims, status, basis, horizon, projection contract, and provenance;
- a complete accessible textual twin and relation inventory;
- report success or failure recorded independently in `result.json` as `Produced(checksum)` or `Failed(receipt/error)`.

Thus my explicit answers are: O1 standoff; O2 two manifest-linked JSON artifacts; O3 Codex plus a separate Atlas, with a bounded layout spike; O4 round-trippable semantics and a non-round-trippable but certifiable pure-HTML/CSS report.

No implementation, child-bead creation, or Stage 1b bypass is authorized by this disposition.
